messages:
alex: Quick async check-in — KMS rotation dry-run completed in prod-candidate cluster last night. No data access incidents, but saw 502 spikes on a small subset of inference requests. Started a rollback for two nodes.

maya: Thanks. I pulled logs — looks like vault-agent restarted while pods were pulling keys. Link: https://internal.corp/logs/3223 (mock)

owen: Which service hit the 502s? Could be token caching TTL.

alex: rtr-service (inference routing shard 7). Error snippet:
```
2026-03-15T02:34:12Z error: kvcache miss, vault connect timeout: dial tcp 10.0.0.7:8200: i/o timeout
```

sam: FYI my PR #4127 (iam: tighten AssumeRole) is blocked by this — need to ensure default role mapping exists after rotation. Pinged in PR for required change.

maya: @sam I can add a fallback mapping to the operator config. Will open a tiny PR today.

li: Reminder — SOC2 checklist item 3.2: confirm key rotation logs retained 90 days. I captured events to s3: s3://redwood-logs/kms-rotations/3223344556/

security-bot: ci/cd: redeploy jobs: https://ci.redwood.dev/builds/98765 — all checks passed except infra-integration (flaky).

owen: Blockers for today: 1) investigate token cache TTL on rtr-service; 2) review sam's PR; 3) run a scoped load test on shard 7 to reproduce 502 and validate rollback.

alex: I'll take the load test. Maya — can you do the fallback mapping PR? If you need help, tag me. We'll reconvene in this thread with short updates.

maya: On it, will open PR in 30m :thumbsup:

sam: Thanks — leaving a review note on the PR template for the default role mapping. ETA EOD.

li: I'll verify retention logs and attach evidence to the SOC2 page.

alex: Cool. No other blockers from my side. If we hit same 502s after fallback, we'll escalate and open an incident channel.

security-bot: docket: rotation-dryrun-3223344556 logged by alex
